channel.title: Silas Johansson: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in Silas Johansson: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends

item.title: Jake E. Lee Shares the Final Text Meessage He Got From Ozzy Osbourne Before His Death
item.description: Jake E. Lee, former guitarist for Ozzy Osbourne, has shared the final message he received from his old bandmate shortly before Osbourne’s death at 76. The two briefly reconnected during Back to the Beginning, the farewell show for Black Sabbath, held at Villa Park in Birmingham.

item.title: MÖTLEY CRÜE's NIKKI SIXX Wants to Live to 100 and 'Outlive His Critics' Along the Way
item.description: Nikki Sixx isn’t just chasing the next riff anymore. NOPE! These days, he’s got his sights set on something a bit more ambitious than a chart position or a sold-out arena, he’s aiming for triple digits.

item.title: HALESTORM Drops New Song 'RAIN YOUR BLOOD ON ME' From Upcoming Album 'EVEREST'
item.description: Halestorm has released a new single titled “Rain Your Blood On Me,” giving fans another preview of the band’s next studio album, Everest, due out August 8 through Atlantic Records (listen below).

item.title: Watch AC/DC Live in Düsseldorf Featuring Angus Young, Brian Johnson, and New Touring Members
item.description: Hard rock icons AC/DC played to a packed stadium in Düsseldorf, Germany, on July 8. The concert took place at Merkur Spiel-Arena as part of the band’s summer 2025 leg of the “Power Up” European tour.

item.title: JACK BLACK Covers 'MR. CROWLEY' with Young Rock Musicians in Tribute to OZZY OSBOURNE; VIDEO
item.description: Jack Black paid tribute to Ozzy Osbourne with a dramatic performance of “Mr. Crowley”, recorded on video and played during the Back to the Beginning event in Birmingham, England, on Saturday, July 5.

item.title: DISTURBED's DAVID DRAIMAN Booed by Some Fans at BLACK SABBATH's Final Show; VIDEO
item.description: Disturbed’s frontman David Draiman stepped onto the stage at Back to the Beginning, the all-star farewell concert for Ozzy Osbourne and Black Sabbath, and was met with a crowd that didn’t quite know how to respond (watch below).

item.title: Watch OZZY OSBOURNE and BLACK SABBATH Reunite for Final Performance at 'Back to the Beginning' in Birmingham
item.description: Ozzy Osbourne gave his final live performance on Saturday, July 5, during the Back to the Beginning event at Villa Park in Birmingham, U.K. The 76-year-old singer took the stage seated on a black throne, delivering a five-song set with his solo band.

item.title: The Demos BLACK SABBATH Recorded Before They Were Famous Are Finally Coming Out
item.description: Before the world knew them as Black Sabbath, the band that helped define heavy metal was just four young musicians from Birmingham, England, playing under the name Earth.

item.title: Spinal Tap Director ROB REINER Calls BLACK SABBATH 'Dumb' Over Stonehenge Accusation: 'It’s Ridiculous'
item.description: The director behind This Is Spinal Tap is calling out Black Sabbath for something that happened over 40 years ago, and he’s not pulling any punches. In a recent interview with Screen Rant, filmmaker Rob Reiner revisited a long-standing misunderstanding between the legendary heavy metal band and the makers of the cult comedy film.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD Hated The Direction Metallica Took In The ‘90s: 'So Stupid'
item.description: In a 2001 interview with Playboy, Metallica frontman James Hetfield reflected on the band’s major style shift during the Load era. For Hetfield, that period, complete with designer clothes, makeup, and fashionable haircuts, wasn’t exactly a high point.

item.title: GLASTONBURY FESTIVAL Condemns BOB VYLAN Performance: 'We are appalled by the statements made', Police Investigating
item.description: Glastonbury Festival organizers have issued a public statement criticizing punk duo Bob Vylan after their controversial set on Saturday. The performance included political messages, a chant targeting the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF), and comments that festival leaders say went too far.

item.title: The Song That Annoyed JAMES HETFIELD, but METALLICA Covered Anyway: 'It Drove Me Nuts'
item.description: James Hetfield has built a career on intensity and control, but even he has moments where personal taste takes a back seat. One of those moments came in the late 1990s, when Metallica recorded “Turn the Page” for their 1998 cover album Garage Inc.

item.title: LIMP BIZKIT’s WES BORLAND’s Controversial Take on Heavy Metal: 'Boring As F*ck'
item.description: Wes Borland, guitarist for Limp Bizkit, has never exactly fit the mold of a typical nü-metal poster boy. Known for his elaborate stage costumes and artistic detours, Borland has always appeared slightly out of place next to Fred Durst’s red Yankees cap and the band’s frat-rap aggression.

item.title: DIMMU BORGIR Announces New Guitarist Kjell Åge “Damage” Karlsen Ahead of Tons of Rock Festival
item.description: Norwegian metal band Dimmu Borgir has a new guitarist. The group announced that Kjell Åge “Damage” Karlsen has joined their lineup. He played his first show with the band on June 27 at the Tons of Rock festival in Oslo, Norway (watch it below).

item.title: Former Comeback Kid bassist Matt Keil diagnosed with ALS, family launches GoFundMe
item.description: Matt Keil, who played bass and shared vocal duties in Comeback Kid between 2008 and 2014, has been diagnosed with ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis). His family confirmed the diagnosis came in May 2024.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Breaks Down the Goal of New METALLICA Doc: 'Turn The Spotlight Away From Us And Celebrate The Fans'
item.description: Metallica’s Lars Ulrich wants people to know the band isn’t the main focus of their new documentary. The real stars, he says, are the fans. Speaking on the red carpet at the Tribeca Festival premiere of Metallica Saved My Life, Ulrich explained why the film shifts attention away from the band and onto the people who have supported them for more than four decades.

item.title: JACOBY SHADDIX Talks New PAPA ROACH Single With TOBY MORSE: 'It Felt Urgent, Honest, In Your Face'
item.description: Papa Roach is back with a new single, and they’ve brought along a longtime friend. The California rock band just released “Braindead” (watch it below), a high-energy track featuring Toby Morse, the lead singer of punk band H2O.

item.title: SHARON OSBOURNE Talks OZZY’s Farewell Show: 'He Didn't Get To Say Goodbye'
item.description: Black Sabbath is officially preparing for its final show with original singer Ozzy Osbourne. The band shared a new photo of Ozzy, bassist Geezer Butler, and drummer Bill Ward in a rehearsal studio (See the photo at the end of the article).

item.title: What Growing Up Was Like for DAVE MUSTAINE: 'My Dad Drank A Lot And Was Abusive'
item.description: Dave Mustaine, the founder of Megadeth and one of heavy metal’s most recognizable voices, has lived a life filled with music, fame, and success. But behind the guitars and sold-out shows is a past that’s far less glamorous.

item.title: KITTIE’s MORGAN LANDER Talks About Writing 'FIRE': 'It Was A Relearning Curve'
item.description: Getting back in the studio after more than a decade isn’t as simple as picking up where you left off. Just ask Morgan Lander. The guitarist and vocalist for Canadian metal band KITTIE says that writing Fire, their first album in 13 years, didn’t come with muscle memory (via TotalRock).

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD Reveals How the 'Terrible' LARS ULRICH Convinced Him to Start METALLICA
item.description: James Hetfield remembers the first time he met Lars Ulrich. According to him, Lars wasn’t exactly a great drummer when they crossed paths. Still, something about his energy made a lasting impression.

item.title: AVRIL LAVIGNE And DERYCK WHIBLEY Reunite Onstage 15 Years After Divorce
item.description: Avril Lavigne brought a familiar face on stage during her set at the Vans Warped Tour 30th anniversary show in Washington, DC this past Sunday. The surprise guest?

item.title: RINGO STARR Slams ROGER DALTREY Over Firing Of Son: 'Never Liked How That Little Man Runs The Band'
item.description: Zak Starkey didn’t bother hiding his disappointment after being pushed out of The Who, a gig he held for nearly 30 years as the band’s live drummer. It all unraveled after a messy show at the Royal Albert Hall earlier this year, which ultimately triggered the official announcement of his departure in April.

item.title: LARS ULRICH Says Younger Fans Ignore METALLICA Classics: 'They're More Into the New Stuff'
item.description: Not every Metallica fan has Master of Puppets tattooed on their brain. According to Lars Ulrich, a surprising number of listeners are skipping the band’s old-school thrash masterpieces in favor of more recent material.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE Recalls METALLICA Audition: 'My Mom Used To Clean Lars' Apartment'
item.description: Dave Mustaine didn’t need to strike a single chord to sense the outcome of his audition for Metallica. After spotting their ad in a magazine, he reached out to Lars Ulrich and arranged to meet up in Newport Beach for a live tryout.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On Metallica T-Shirts: 'I’m Not Sure I Want Them Wearing That'
item.description: Plenty of metalheads have their rituals. They blast albums, whether on vinyl, cassette, or whatever streaming service rules the moment. They pack venues when the tour bus rolls into town.

item.title: Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit" Surpasses 2 Billion YouTube Views
item.description: Nirvana’s “Smells Like Teen Spirit” has now passed the 2-billion view mark on YouTube. After first being uploaded in 2009, the video quietly amassed its first billion by 2019.

item.title: Is Slipknot Releasing a New Album in 2025? Here’s What We Know So Far
item.description: Slipknot fans are eagerly awaiting news of the band’s next studio album following 2022’s The End, So Far. While a new record hasn’t been officially announced, the band members have dropped numerous hints in recent interviews about their plans.

item.title: DISTURBED to Release New Single "I Will Not Break" on February 21, 2025; Everything We Know So Far
item.description: Aight listen up. This Friday—February 21, 2025—DISTURBED is unleashing a brand-new single, “I Will Not Break,” and from the unhinged energy flying around the internet, you’d think it was the Second Coming… of Ten Thousand Fists or Indestructible or Asylum or whatever era of DISTURBED your uncle with a Tapout shirt refuses to shut up about.

item.title: Killswitch Engage’s Mike D’Antonio Rejects A.I. Claims: "I Don’t Wanna Be Associated With It"
item.description: Another day, another internet conspiracy theory—this time, aimed at Killswitch Engage bassist and graphic designer Mike D’Antonio, who’s had to crawl out of the art cave he’s been living in for the past eight months just to tell people to shut the hell up about A.

item.title: Jethro Tull’s Ian Anderson Slams Brazilian Fans & iPhones: "Crowds Are Worse Than Ever"
item.description: So Ian Anderson, flute-wielding sorcerer of JETHRO TULL, has had it with you people—yes, YOU, the one recording an entire concert through a cracked iPhone 8 with 2% battery while also screaming “PLAY THICK AS A BRICK!

item.title: Arch Enemy Drops "Paper Tiger" Music Video and Reveals Blood Dynasty Tour Dates
item.description: Ok SO listen—Arch Enemy decided that the world needed to be LOUDER, and who are we to argue??? They dropped “Paper Tiger” and I swear to Odin’s beard it’s got that Judas Priest but also Arch Enemy but also maybe a bit of an angry chainsaw vibe.

item.title: Grammy Interviewer Mistakes Spiritbox’s Courtney LaPlante for Poppy—See the Full Video
item.description: Yeah babe, the Grammys. A night of glitz, glamour, and—if we’re being honest—rock and metal getting shoved to the side like an unwanted side dish at a fancy dinner.

item.title: Cult Metal Band SACRED BLADE Reunites for Live Show and Album Reissue; “This is long overdue!” says Robertson
item.description: SACRED BLADE, a name spoken in hushed tones in Canadian metal lore, is back. After 20 years of silence, the Vancouver legends are set to play again—kicking things off at Germany’s Keep It True festival on April 25, 2025.

item.title: John Corabi on Mötley Crüe Exit: "Relieved and Bummed"
item.description: John Corabi (yes, the guy who briefly fronted Mötley Crüe) sat down for an interview and spilled—well, not tea exactly, but maybe lukewarm coffee. His time with the band?

item.title: Slipknot's Look Outside Your Window Finally Set for 2025 Release
item.description: Slipknot’s Look Outside Your Window is like Bigfoot. Always talked about. Never seen. But now, after nearly 20 years of “soon, we swear,” the album might actually happen.

item.title: Watch: Brandon Toews Masters LINKIN PARK’s From Zero in Record Time
item.description: Linkin Park has thrown their latest creation, From Zero, into the wild, and someone thought it’d be a good idea to see if a drummer could tackle the whole thing on the fly.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda Talks Brad Delson’s Tour Absence
item.description: Linkin Park’s reunion, complete with a fresh album release last Friday, has been making waves. Yet, the band’s current lineup feels like a revolving door. With Chester Bennington’s tragic loss in 2017 and drummer Rob Bourdon sitting this one out, it’s already a scaled-back return.

item.title: Linkin Park Announces 2025 Global Tour Across 50+ Cities
item.description: It looks like Linkin Park has made good on their not-so-subtle hints and officially announced a globe-trotting tour to support their upcoming album, From Zero, set to drop this Friday.

item.title: European Tour Canceled as As I Lay Dying Faces Major Member Departures
item.description: It’s a mass exodus over in the As I Lay Dying camp, with members dropping off faster than you can say “farewell tour.” The band’s entire European tour is scrapped, and not a peep has come from the remaining members—whoever’s still sticking around, that is.

item.title: Static-X: No Full Albums, But Maybe Singles, Says Tony Campos
item.description: Tony Campos isn’t pulling any punches when it comes to the future of Static-X. In a recent chat with Nikki Blakk from 107.7 The Bone, Campos laid it out: as long as they’re having fun and the fans keep showing up, the band will keep going.

item.title: John 5 Breaks Silence on Relationship With Rob Zombie After Joining Mötley Crüe
item.description: John 5, the guy who’s jumped from Rob Zombie’s ship straight into the glam-coated arms of Mötley Crüe, apparently hasn’t had a real chat with Zombie since his departure.

item.title: James Hetfield: "We Don’t Want to Be a Legacy Band That Only Plays Hits"
item.description: METALLICA’s James Hetfield has made it pretty clear that they’re not interested in simply coasting on past glories. In an interview on “The Metallica Report”—that podcast where the band gives you a peek behind the curtain—James laid it out.

item.title: Korn and Adidas Pay Tribute to 1994 with New Superstar Shoes
item.description: Korn and Adidas have once again teamed up, this time with a new Superstar shoe drop. It’s about as surprising as the sun rising—anyone who’s been around long enough knows this collab was practically written in the stars.

item.title: Linkin Park's Mike Shinoda: "This Isn’t a Reunion, It’s a New Chapter"
item.description: Mike Shinoda recently shared more details about Linkin Park’s reformation during an interview with BBC Radio 1’s New Music Show With Jack Saunders. The vocalist and multi-instrumentalist pulled back the curtain on how the band’s new chapter began and what fans can expect moving forward.

item.title: As I Lay Dying: 'We Are The Dead' Drops with Alex Terrible and Tom Barber; VIDEO
item.description: As I Lay Dying is gearing up to drop their latest album, Through Storms Ahead, set to land on November 15. Nestled among the tracks are “Burden,” “The Cave We Fear to Enter,” and the freshly unleashed “We Are The Dead.

item.title: Robert Trujillo Calls Metallica Bass Position the “Most Demanding Gig”
item.description: Robert Trujillo might be the newest face on the Metallica bass, but with two decades under his belt, he’s hardly the fresh recruit anymore. Slotting in as the fourth bassist after Jason Newsted, the legendary Cliff Burton, and, yes, the lesser-known Ron McGovney (check Wikipedia if you must), Trujillo’s view of the job is clear: playing bass for Metallica is no walk in the park.

item.title: Slipknot's Mask Maker Crafts Demonic Masks for Shin Megami Tensei V
item.description: Some collaborations leave you scratching your head, and this one’s no exception. Slipknot, the metal world’s masked enigma, has somehow found itself linked to Atlus, the studio behind the Shin Megami Tensei series.

item.title: Eloy Casagrande’s First Gig with Slipknot Leaves Fans in Awe
item.description: Slipknot’s newest recruit, Eloy Casagrande, hasn’t had much time to catch his breath. His debut as the band’s drummer wasn’t just any gig—it was a small, fiery show staged in a Californian desert venue that probably violates more safety codes than your local dive bar.

item.title: Metallica Sets New Attendance Record at St. Louis Dome; See Details
item.description: Metallica has managed to once again defy expectations by packing out St. Louis’ Dome at America’s Center, showing that even after decades in the game, they’re still pulling crowds that could rival any pop superstar.

item.title: Metallica Files Lawsuit to Halt Bootleg Sales Before St. Louis Concert
item.description: Metallica’s merchandise machine is back at it, keeping the unauthorized sellers in check before they even get a shot at making a quick buck off their name. This time, their touring merch partner, Merch Traffic, has filed a lawsuit in St.

item.title: Metallica’s "Nothing Else Matters" Reaches 1 Billion Streams on Spotify
item.description: Metallica’s “Nothing Else Matters” has now crossed the monumental 1 billion streams mark on Spotify. This track, from the band’s blockbuster 1991 self-titled album, divides opinions like few others.

item.title: Jordan Mancino Steps Back: As I Lay Dying Faces Internal Challenges
item.description: The chaos surrounding As I Lay Dying just keeps piling up. After Josh Gilbert made his grand exit, the band scrambled to patch things together by roping in Ryan Neff of Miss May I to cover bass and vocals, while Ken Susi of Unearth stepped in on guitar.
